”

pages.en:
…The body in my arms is impossibly heavy.

Is she this heavy because she no longer has the strength to stand, or can she no longer stand because her body has become so heavy?

Either way, Sakura's fever has left her unable to walk without help, and she alone believes she is well.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…I support her, but her body is heavy.
She must not have the power to stand up, or maybe she can’t stand up because her body is heavy.
Either way, Sakura’s so sick that she can’t walk by herself, and she’s the only one who thinks she’s fine.

By the time I bring her there, Sakura is already asleep.

Though “asleep” may be the wrong word. She seems half conscious still.

Her breathing is labored, and once—only once—her hand closes tightly around the arm holding her.

She’s breathing painfully and takes a firm grip on my arm.

Fortunately, her breathing has begun to settle now that she is lying down. Something to bring down the fever should be enough to help her recover.

Once she can walk on her own again, I can take her to the hospital and have them prescribe something for the cold.

pages.en:
On the way to school, I stop at Fuji's house and arrange for one of their housekeepers to come over.

Fuji dresses so casually that I sometimes forget it, but the Fujimura household is one of the two wealthiest families in this neighborhood.

I drop by Fuji-nee’s place on my way to school to have their housekeeper come by.
I sometimes forget because Fuji-nee’s not the type to dress up, but the Fujimura family is one of the richest households around here.

pages.en:
They are not even a company, yet they have dozens of hard-faced men they call “employees.”

Most of them live in the detached buildings on the Fujimura estate, which makes it a very large household indeed.

Naturally, they employ a matching number of domestic staff, so if we ask, they can usually spare a housekeeper who is not otherwise occupied.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It has dozens of scary-looking people that call themselves company employees even though it’s not even a company.
Many of them live in the outbuilding, so they are a large family.
So there are many housekeepers, and one will be free to spare if I ask.

pages.en:
—And so.

They agree to send over the woman who helped me through emergencies several times before Sakura began coming to the house.

She and Sakura already know each other. I should be able to leave Sakura in her care without worry.
